newsitem.title: UK: Golf-Ten teams still hopeful of Dunhill Cup success.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Ten teams still hopeful of Dunhill Cup success.

text.p: Ten teams, including 1,000-1 outsiders India, can still qualify on Saturday for the Alfred Dunhill Cup semifinals.
The Indian debutants' 2-1 destruction of Scotland's hopes of retaining the title on Friday left them with an outside shot at a place in the last four.

But they will need a 3-0 win over group two pacesetters Sweden to go through -- a tall order, particularly in light of Ali Sher's 84 in cold, windy conditions on Friday that are forecast to continue over the weekend.
Sweden, winner of both their ties so far, need only win one of the three matches with India to advance.
In group one, the top-seeded United States, eighth-seeded Spain and unseeded England can all win, though the Americans are in the driving seat.
If they beat Spain they advance. If they lose 2-1 to Spain they still go through if Italy beat England.
England can win the group if they beat Italy and Spain beat the United States 3-0. Spain take it if they beat the Americans 3-0 and England lose to Italy.

Second-seeded Australia are almost assured of advancing from group four, unless they repeat last year's feat and lose their third round-robin tie 3-0. A 2-1 defeat by New Zealand would still take Australia through.
New Zealand must win 3-0 and hope Japan do not beat Germany 3-0 if they are to reach the last four.
Japan's outside chance depends on their beating Germany 3-0 and New Zealand whitewashing Australia.
The most straightforward group is the third, where South Africa and Ireland, seeded third and sixth, have each won twice.
Whichever side wins their tie will go through.
